name: North Face

pitch_detail.notes: Four pitches up the prominent central chimney splitting the north face.
Exit left onto an exposed rib for three pitches of delicate face climbing, then a gully with large chockstones to the summit.

approach: Approached through Davis Peak's northern cirque from the Stetattle Creek side, north of the peak; no detailed trailhead-to-base mileage is recorded.
overview: A serious, rarely-repeated alpine rock route up Davis Peak's huge north-facing cirque wall: four pitches up a prominent central chimney system, then three pitches out onto an exposed rib of delicate face climbing, finishing through a gully choked with large chockstones to the summit.
beta: The route climbs the northern cirque by its prominent central chimney system for four pitches, then exits left onto an exposed rib for three pitches of delicate face climbing before re-entering a gully choked with very large chockstones that leads to the top near the summit. The chimney is probably a melted-out form of the older Kloke-Simon couloir line. About 4,000 ft of climbing; part of the first ascent was done by moonlight.
